name: Week 16 KB Saturday Cardio — Conditioning (Spotlight: Snatch; 100-Rep Block Finisher)
description: Saturday KB OPTION — pure conditioning, distinct from Tue (strength) and Thu (lighter skill template). Light bell throughout (16-20lb) — breathing rate and sustainability are the targets, not load. The Asgooch cardio complex carries over; the flow combos rotate to halo→reverse-lunge + around-the-body-pass-to-squat; and the finisher rotates this week to high-rep 100-rep blocks (from the @gymfiesta daily challenge) — light bell, posture-and-volume focused. Spotlight on the snatch (the technical, shoulder-relevant move in the cardio complex). Choice-of-the-day on D6 alongside stairmaster, easy run, or rest.

dayOverview.theme: Saturday conditioning — light bell, breathing-rate target. Asgooch cardio complex + rotated flow combos. Finisher rotates to 100-rep blocks. Day after Friday legs — squatting stays LIGHT on purpose. Spotlight: the snatch punch-through.

spotlights.why: The technical centerpiece of the Asgooch cardio complex and the most right-shoulder-relevant move on a light-bell day. Spotlight the hip-drive + punch-through + soft catch so the bell doesn't bang the wrist or crash the shoulder at the top — the move that most rewards clean mechanics on a conditioning day.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W14 controlled-power finisher · W15 brutal-complex-variant finisher · W16 100-rep block finisher (current) · W17 cycle forward — controlled-power or a fresh complex. The Asgooch cardio complex stays; the flow combos + finisher rotate so Saturday stays fresh.
watchpoints: **Day after Friday legs.** Squatting (front squat × 6 in the complex) stays LIGHT — 16-20lb. The 100-rep finisher is upper/core/hinge biased on purpose; skip the squat reps if the QL/quads are talking.
**Light bell is the whole point** — 16-20lb working. Conditioning means breathing rate, not bell weight.
**Asgooch CARDIO complex ≠ Tuesday's OVERHEAD complex** — same author, different chain. Cardio = row/clean/squat/snatch (low-and-explosive).
**Snatch spotlight** — hips drive the bell, punch the hand THROUGH at the top for a soft catch, no bang on the wrist. Sub high pulls if the right shoulder crackles on the catch.
**Finisher rotated to 100-rep blocks** — light bell, 4×25 each. Break to 5×20 if needed. It's posture + volume conditioning, not strength; keep moving.
**Choice-of-the-day on D6** — not mandatory. Skip if Friday legs cooked you; swap for stairmaster / easy run if cardio-only is the call. No pull-up greasing here — Saturday is the conditioning flank.

Easy two-handed swings. Prime the hinge.
Light, open the hips. Skip if Friday legs left the quads sore.
Standing, torso hinged slightly forward. Wakes the grip + forearm + posterior chain — primes the snatch catch.

sets.name: 🔆 Asgooch Cardio Complex — LEFT (Spotlight: Snatch)

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 16-20lb. Left hand. Hips back, back flat, pull the elbow past the ribs. 2s pull, 2s lower.
Left hand. **Hip drive into the rack** — thumb to collarbone. Smooth catch — knees absorb.
Left rack. **LIGHT** — Friday legs is yesterday. Sit tall, full depth IF the legs are fresh; reduce depth before load if they're cooked.

Left hand. 🔆 **SPOTLIGHT — the punch-through:**
- **Hips drive the bell**, not the arm — the hinge throws it overhead
- **Punch the hand THROUGH at the top** — the bell rotates around the wrist and you punch up to meet it, so it settles soft with no bang
- **Soft catch, ribs down at lockout** — the bell stacks over the shoulder
- **Right shoulder watch on the catch** — sub high pulls for the last 2 rounds if it crackles

sets.notes: 5 rounds LEFT. Continuous within a round — row → clean → squat → snatch with no rest. Rest 30-45s between rounds. **Weak side first.** Different from Tuesday's overhead Asgooch — same author, different chain.

sets.name: Asgooch Cardio Complex — RIGHT

exercises.notes: Right hand. Same form — hips back, full extension.
Right hand. Smooth clean to the rack.
Right rack. Same depth/load discipline as the left.
Right hand. **Spotlight punch-through + right shoulder watchpoint on the catch** — same modify-to-high-pull rule.

sets.notes: 5 rounds RIGHT. Continuous within a round. **If the workout is running long after the left side, drop to 3-4 rounds right — don't grind a quality session into a sloppy one.**

sets.name: Flow Combos — Halo to Reverse Lunge + Around-the-Body Pass to Squat

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 16-20lb. Halo one direction → reverse lunge → halo the other direction → reverse lunge the other leg. Continuous, fluid. The halo loosens the shoulder while the lunge keeps the legs honest.

Pass the bell around the body once → squat → next pass, alternating pass direction. Torso tall and still during the pass; full depth on the squat (LIGHT — Friday legs is yesterday). Coordination + conditioning hybrid.

sets.notes: Coordination-conditioning hybrids — the upper-body skill challenge slows the leg work down enough that the squats don't dump the quads. 3 rounds, 30-45s rest between rounds.

sets.name: 🌀 100-Rep Block Finisher — Light & High-Volume (Rotated In for W16)

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 16-20lb. Pass the bell around the hips/body, alternate direction each set. Core tight, torso quiet. 4×25 = 100 total.
Side-to-side swings across the body — use core rotation, hips drive. 4×25 = 100 total.
Explosive hip snap, pull the bell to chin height, elbows high. 4×25 = 100 total. **Right shoulder watch** — keep it light; the hip snap does the work, not the arm.
Standard two-handed swings — squeeze the glutes hard at the top, keep the hinge honest as the reps climb. 4×25 = 100 total.

sets.notes: **100-rep block finisher — light bell, high volume.** Four blocks of 100 (4×25 each = 400 reps). Break each 100 into 4×25 or 5×20 as needed; rest 20-30s between blocks. **If short on time or pre-fatigued, do the first 2-3 blocks** — don't grind the volume into sloppy reps. Posture + conditioning, not strength; keep moving and keep the breathing rate up.

tips: **Saturday conditioning option — choice-of-the-day on D6.** Alternates with stairmaster, easy run, or rest. Skip if Friday legs cooked you.
**LIGHT bell throughout: 16-20lb working.** This is the whole point. Conditioning = breathing rate, not load.
**Core blocks carry over:** Asgooch CARDIO complex (row/clean/squat/snatch × 6 × 5 rounds per side) + rotated flow combos (halo→reverse-lunge + around-body-pass→squat).
**Finisher rotated to 100-rep blocks** — around-body pass / side swing / high pull / swing, 4×25 each, light bell. Do 2-3 blocks if short on time.
**Spotlight: the snatch punch-through** — hips drive, punch the hand through, soft catch. Sub high pulls if the catch crackles.
**Squatting stays LIGHT** — Friday legs is yesterday. Skip the squat reps if the quads are tight.
**Right shoulder watch on the snatch + high pull** — light bell, smooth catch; high pulls if it crackles.
**No pull-up greasing here** — Saturday is the conditioning flank.
Rotation plan: W17 rotates the finisher again so Saturday stays fresh.
formPhilosophy: Saturday is conditioning, distinct from the Tue and Thu KB days. Light bell, more reps, more variety. The cave-pull strategy rotates the finisher block week to week — controlled-power, brutal-complex, now 100-rep blocks — so Saturday builds breadth without going stale or heavy. The day stays explicitly optional: it's the KB flavor of the D6 cardio choice, for days when a treadmill isn't the right call.
